To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the epithelioidal vascular tumors EHE, and EAS, express the endothelial markers, vimentin, and keratin, but not the epithelial markers CEA, or EMA.
epithelioid angioendothelioma and epithelioid angisarcoma may express keratin, in addition to the endothelial markers, factor VIII and UEA-1.

the epithelioidal hemangioendotheioma and epithelioidal angiosarcoma, in addition to the endothelial markers FVIII- related antigen, vimentin, and Ulex europaeaus agglutinin 1, express the epithelial keratin marker.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of endothelial- as well as epithelial-associated markers in epithelioid hemangoendothelioma and epithelioid angio sarcoma.
the use of immunohistochemistry to identify and characterize the epithelioid hemangoendothelioma and angiosarcoma.
the use of immunohistochemistry in the diagnosis and classification of soft tissue neoplasms and the role of cytokeratin in the differential diagnosis of epithelioid angioendothelomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

epithelial markers are not reliable for distinguishing vascular neoplasia from carcinoma, and that the presence or absence of keratin staining in vascular tumors is not a reliable marker for distinguishing epithelioid vascular tumor from epithelial neoplasm.
the epithelioids of the epithelioid hemangoendothelioma and epithelioid angiasarcoma can express keratin.
keratin is not expressed in endothelial cells of any vascular tumor, including EHE and EHS, and that its presence in a vascular tumor is diagnostic for a carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epithelial-associated markers keratin and carcinoembryoic antigen are not useful in the diagnosis of epithelioid angioendothelioma and angiosarcoma.
epithelioid vascular tumor may express both endothelial and epithelial markers.
keratin staining in vascular neoplasia may be seen in the epithelioid variant of EHE and EHE, but not in the epitheliold variant of EAS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
keratin staining is not specific for epithelial differentiation and may be seen in vascular tumors, especially those that are epithelioid.
keratin positivity in a soft-tissue tumor does not exclude the diagnosis of an epithelioid vascular tumor.
epithelial-associated markers are not reliable for differentiating epithelial from mesenchymal tumors.
